author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory names every specialty the clinic knows, under its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it. One page, no paging, reachable by its address alone.
acceptance_criteria: GET /specialties.html returns a page naming every specialty the clinic knows, under its stored name
each specialty shows the veterinarians holding it, by first name then last name
a veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on the page
a specialty no veterinarian holds is still listed, with no veterinarian under it
a veterinarian holding more than one specialty appears once under each specialty they hold
every specialty appears on one page and no paging is offered
wording the page introduces is present in every supported language, per REQ-LANG-002
non_goals: managing veterinarians or specialties from this page (NG-2 unchanged)
a navigation entry or a link to this page from anywhere else
any fixed ordering of specialties or of the veterinarians under one
notes: Product owner fixed both scope decisions; not re-litigated. Three open questions recorded in docs/prd.md rather than blocking: a visible entry point (deferred to a follow-up), presentation order, and whether an unheld specialty is marked as such. Narrowest reading taken on each. REQ-SPC-001 is specified, not derived from observed behavior, unlike the rest of this PRD.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice lands entirely inside the existing vet feature package and reuses patterns already in force: feature-package organization, a Spring Data repository per persisted lookup type, a server-rendered Thymeleaf view, and message-bundle wording. One adjustment is required. Vet.specialties is a unidirectional ManyToMany, so vet-side traversal cannot reach a specialty no veterinarian holds; a Specialty-side repository must be added, mirroring PetTypeRepository. The specialty-to-veterinarian inversion goes into one pure value object (SpecialtyHolders) rather than the controller, because architecture-principles.md forbids new business rules in web controllers. docs/system-design.md gained three Contracts rows and one state paragraph; no ADR is warranted.
integration_points: VetController gains @GetMapping("/specialties.html") returning view name vets/specialtyList; it loads, delegates to SpecialtyHolders, and selects the view, holding no rule itself
VetController gains a second constructor argument, SpecialtyRepository; VetControllerTests must supply it or the context fails to start
VetRepository.findAll() is reused as-is and stays @Cacheable("vets"), sharing its single cache entry with the /vets route
new template extends fragments/layout :: layout (~{::body},'specialties'); passing 'specialties' highlights no navigation item, which matches the no-nav-entry scope
new message keys must be added to messages.properties and the nine translated bundles; messages_en.properties stays intentionally empty as the English fallback

patterns.description: precedent for a repository over a persisted lookup value; SpecialtyRepository follows it but extends the narrower org.springframework.data.repository.Repository<Specialty, Integer> like VetRepository, per the minimal-surface principle
existing read-only GET handler shape: repository call, model attributes, view-name return
template shape; every visible string reaches the page through th:text="#{key}" so I18nPropertiesSyncTest passes

Domain service and value object sit in the 'Available, not currently used' catalog; adopting one needs no ADR. SpecialtyHolders is a public immutable record in the vet package, defensively copying its veterinarian list

risks.risk: @Cacheable("specialties") on the new repository fails at runtime: CacheConfiguration creates only the 'vets' cache through the JCache API, and Spring's JCacheCacheManager does not create unknown caches on demand
risks.mitigation: leave SpecialtyRepository uncached; do not widen CacheConfiguration, which would also extend the unresolved vet-cache-eviction open question

risks.risk: grouping veterinarians by Specialty object identity breaks silently: BaseEntity defines no equals/hashCode, so Specialty instances loaded separately, served from the vets cache, or built by a test are never equal
risks.mitigation: key the grouping on specialty.getId(); tests assign ids explicitly, as the existing VetControllerTests factories already do

risks.risk: grouping by specialty name would merge two distinct specialties that share a name; specialties.name carries no unique constraint in any vendor schema
risks.mitigation: key on id, not name; the stored name is presentation only

risks.risk: a package-private model type fails at render time under SpEL property access
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyHolders and its accessors are public; the controller and repository stay package-private and public respectively, as their siblings are

risks.risk: seed data holds no unheld specialty (all three of radiology, surgery, dentistry are held), so the edge case cannot be observed against the real database
risks.mitigation: cover the unheld-specialty and multi-specialty cases in SpecialtyHoldersTests with real objects and no framework context; the web test covers route, view, and one-page rendering

risks.risk: a hard-coded string in the new template fails the build
risks.mitigation: I18nPropertiesSyncTest.checkNonInternationalizedStrings rejects any src/main HTML line with literal text between > and < that carries neither #{ nor th:text; the existing keys specialties, vets, and none already cover the likely wording, and any genuinely new key goes into all ten non-English bundles

notes: Lazy loading is a non-issue: Vet.specialties is FetchType.EAGER and hibernate.default_batch_fetch_size is 16, so the association is initialized before spring.jpa.open-in-view=false closes the session. Do not switch it to LAZY and do not add an @EntityGraph. Cached Vet instances are detached and shared across requests; SpecialtyHolders must read them, never call addSpecialty. No new trust boundary: the route is a parameterless read-only GET, and Thymeleaf's default escaping covers the stored names, so security-principles.md needs no change. NG-2 is untouched. No ADR: every type adopted sits in the architecture-principles catalog, and no hard-to-reverse trade-off is made. Ordering is deliberately unconstrained per the prd-entry non-goals, so tests must not assert an order; Vet.getSpecialties() happens to sort by name. Test placement note for the implementer: the prd-entry file_targets name VetControllerTests.java as the starting set, and the five semantic test names belong on the framework-free SpecialtyHoldersTests, which moves the slice toward the base of the pyramid as testing-principles.md asks; theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldRenderEverySpecialtyOnOnePage stays a web test asserting the model carries every specialty and exposes no paging attributes. New tests use factory methods and BDD names per testing-principles.md. One vocabulary observation for product-requirements-expert, not a blocker: docs/ubiquitous-language.md has no entry for the specialty directory itself, though the PRD names it; the type name SpecialtyHolders derives from the canonical verb in the Specialty entry ('held by zero or more Veterinarians').

author: code-quality-reviewer
approved_aspects: Inversion/grouping logic fully isolated in SpecialtyHolders.directory(), keyed by specialty.getId() per the design constraint (getId() comment explains why, since BaseEntity defines no equals/hashCode)
VetController.showSpecialtyDirectory is a thin delegator with no business rules, consistent with the rest of the controller
SpecialtyRepository extends the narrow Repository<Specialty, Integer>, declares no @Cacheable, and its javadoc explains why (JCache does not autocreate unknown caches)
Vet.specialties EAGER fetch left untouched
specialtyList.html mirrors the existing vetList.html idiom (th:each span + none fallback) and uses only th:text (auto-escaped), no nav entry added per the no-nav constraint
Naming (SpecialtyHolders, 'holds'/'holders') matches docs/ubiquitous-language.md's Specialty/Veterinarian relationship wording
checkFormat task passes clean on the changed files

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Output escaping: src/main/resources/templates/vets/specialtyList.html renders every dynamic value through th:text (specialty.name, vet.firstName/lastName) and message keys through #{}; a repo-wide sweep of src/main/resources/templates/ for th:utext returns no hits, so Thymeleaf default escaping stays on (security-principles.md 'Cross-site scripting' row, system-design.md Threat Model XSS row).

Injection surface: GET /specialties.html is parameterless — no request parameter, path variable, header, or body reaches any code path. Data access is the Spring Data derived query SpecialtyRepository.findAll() plus the existing VetRepository.findAll(); no string-concatenated query text is introduced (security-principles.md 'Injection into data access').

No write path: the only new mapping is @GetMapping; SpecialtyRepository declares findAll() alone under @Transactional(readOnly = true) and exposes no save/delete; a grep of the vet package confirms no mutating annotation or persistence call is added. NG-2 is unchanged.

No mutation of cached detached entities: SpecialtyHolders.directory only reads Vet.getSpecialties(), which returns a fresh sorted list copy, and accumulates references into new local ArrayLists defensively copied by the record's compact constructor (List.copyOf). Cached Vet instances shared across requests are never modified.
Mass assignment: no request-bound type and no data binder are introduced, so the identifier-disallow requirement does not apply to this change.

Information disclosure: the page renders only specialty names and veterinarian full names, both already public through the existing /vets.html and /vets routes. No credential, connection string, identifier, or PII beyond that baseline reaches the rendered page or any error path.
Supply chain: no dependency change — build.gradle, settings.gradle, gradle/, and pom.xml are outside the change set, so no new artifact widens the attack surface and no version needs CVE review.

Exposed surface: one new unauthenticated read-only HTML route on the same open surface as the existing directory pages; no management endpoint exposure is broadened. The application is not left weaker than the system-design.md Security Context baseline.

Unbounded result set: the page is deliberately unpaginated per REQ-SPC-001 and reads two small lookup tables (specialties, vets). Availability-only, matching a PRD-stated requirement — no security finding.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The suite's own docstring says SpecialtyHolders.directory() 'inverts a complete specialty list' and the production code keys its grouping map by Specialty id specifically because 'BaseEntity defines no equals/hashCode, so two instances of one specialty are never equal.' Every existing unit test, however, passes the *same* Specialty object reference into both the specialties collection and the vet's addSpecialty(...) call (e.g. theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldShowEachHoldingVetByFullName: `Specialty radiology = createASpecialty(RADIOLOGY); Vet helen = createAVet("Helen", "Leary", radiology);` then `SpecialtyHolders.directory(List.of(radiology), List.of(helen))`). Reference equality would pass every one of these tests just as well as id-based equality, so the hazard the production comment calls out — two detached instances of the same specialty, as happens when a vet's cached specialty and the repository's specialty list are loaded independently — is claimed but not exercised. A regression that swapped the map key from `held.getId()` to `held` (or to the Specialty object itself) would not be caught by this file.
findings.fix: Add a test that constructs two distinct Specialty instances sharing one id (e.g. two separate `createASpecialty(...)` calls followed by manually setting the same id, or a factory overload `createASpecialty(id, name)`), passes one instance in the specialties list and the other instance (attached to a vet) in the veterinarians list, and asserts the vet is grouped under that specialty — proving the grouping is by id, not object identity.

findings.description: theSpecialtyDirectoryPageShouldShowEachHoldingVetByFullName only asserts content().string(containsString("Helen Leary")) anywhere on the page. It does not verify Helen is listed under radiology specifically (vs. surgery, or floating outside any specialty block), so a bug that put her name in the wrong section, or duplicated her under every specialty, would not be caught. This test also happens to be the only place in the diff where two distinct Specialty instances sharing id=1 flow through directory() (helen() calls radiology() internally for her held specialty, and setup() separately calls radiology() for specialties.findAll()), which is the detached-instance scenario the unit suite is missing — but the weak assertion here means this incidental coverage does not actually prove correct-section placement, only presence somewhere on the page.
findings.fix: Scope the assertion to the specialty section, e.g. assert the rendered HTML fragment under the radiology heading contains "Helen Leary" and the surgery section does not, using a targeted content().string(matchesPattern(...)) or an HtmlUnit/Jsoup-based structural assertion instead of a page-wide containsString.

approved_aspects: SpecialtyHoldersTests.java is framework-free, uses real Vet/Specialty objects with no mocking, follows four-phase structure with blank-line separation, uses AssertJ fluent assertions throughout (extracting/flatExtracting/containsExactlyInAnyOrder), and avoids asserting any fixed order on the top-level directory list per the PRD's non-goal

All PRD acceptance criteria (unheld specialty listed, no-specialty vet omitted, multi-specialty vet appears under each, full-name first-then-last, single page/no paging) have a dedicated test each, matching the planned test_names from the prd-entry

Test pyramid shape is good for this slice: the new domain rule (specialty inversion) lives in a pure unit test class (SpecialtyHoldersTests, no I/O), with only the two necessary web-layer checks added to the existing MockMvc-based VetControllerTests, consistent with testing-principles.md's guidance to push logic-heavy tests to the base of the pyramid
Coverage is 100% line/branch on SpecialtyHolders.java and VetController.java per jacocoTestReport, well above the 80% domain-package target

VetControllerTests' continued use of @MockitoBean on VetRepository/SpecialtyRepository is consistent with the brief's pre-existing-suite exemption (mocking only at the pre-existing pattern, not a new violation introduced by this slice)
./gradlew test passes cleanly for both changed test files

author: doc-reviewer

findings.description: The new Specialty directory prose states the literal route "/specialties.html" ("The page is reached at its own address, `/specialties.html`, and nothing links to it"). This is a PRD-boundary violation: a hardcoded HTTP route is mechanism, not behavior. It also breaks the established convention in this same PRD — the sibling Veterinarian directory section (REQ-VET-001) never states its literal path "/vets.html" in prose, and even docs/system-design.md avoids stating literal route strings for either page (it says "a second vet route", "a third route", never the literal path). The "Done when" bullet for this same requirement already gets it right ("opens the directory's address directly", no literal string). Rewrite the narrative sentence to match: state that the page is reachable at an address of its own with no inbound link, without the literal path. If the literal path needs to be on record, it belongs in system-design.md, matching how the Vet route is (not) recorded there.

"Specialty directory" is introduced and used repeatedly as a named capability (prd.md heading, narrative, three Done-when bullets, an Open Question — 5+ uses; system-design.md package-structure line and the new state paragraph above the Contracts table) but has no entry in docs/ubiquitous-language.md. The sibling term "veterinarian directory" has the same gap, but this change compounds it by minting a second undefined "X directory" term rather than resolving it. Per the Cross-Document Coherence checklist, a domain term used in prd.md and system-design.md must be defined in ubiquitous-language.md in the same change. Add a "Specialty directory" (and ideally "Veterinarian directory") entry to docs/ubiquitous-language.md.

author: change-grader
summary: add the read-only specialty directory page

blast_radius.note: Nine files but a contained landing: one new GET route, one new repository, one new pure value object, all inside the existing vet feature package, plus three docs and one template. The only edit to existing production code is VetController gaining a second constructor argument, and VetController is package-private with no other construction site in the tree. No schema, dependency, config, or sensitive-path change; the extractor reports zero sensitive paths.

semantic_surprise.note: The hunks do exactly what the description implies. SpecialtyHolders.directory keys its grouping map on held.getId() with a comment explaining why (BaseEntity defines no equals/hashCode, specialties.name has no unique constraint), reads Vet.getSpecialties() without mutating cached detached instances, and List.copyOf in the compact constructor makes the record genuinely immutable. The template renders every dynamic value through th:text, so escaping stays on. Existing vet-list behavior is untouched. The one plan-versus-diff discrepancy is benign and I checked it by hand: the design named messages.properties and nine translated bundles as targets, yet no bundle changed, because the template mints no new key and specialties, name, vets, and none already exist in all ten non-English bundles.

test_adequacy.note: Tests assert real outcomes rather than restating the implementation. SpecialtyHoldersTests is framework-free over real Vet and Specialty objects and covers each acceptance criterion, including the unheld specialty and the multi-specialty vet. The round-two addition is the load-bearing one: theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldShowAHoldingVetWhoseSpecialtyIsASeparateInstance builds two distinct Specialty instances sharing an id, so reverting the map key from held.getId() to the object would fail it. The web test now scopes its assertion to the specialty's table row, proving section placement rather than page-wide presence.

reviewer_hedging.note: The risk plan dispatched the full battery and all four reviewers ended approved with empty findings lists, no escalate tag and no residual caveat. The four round-one bar_clause findings were substantively re-verified rather than waved through, the test-reviewer by a hand mutation check and the doc-reviewer by greps against the document's own convention. One process note surfaced inside an approval, system-design-expert writing docs/ubiquitous-language.md outside its normal write scope, which the author flagged openly and the reviewer judged not to affect correctness.

scope_deviation.note: Zero build retries, zero consultations, zero design revisions: the slice never fought its triage. The diff stays on the requirement's stated surface, read-only with no nav entry, no inbound link and no paging, and NG-2 is untouched since the new repository declares findAll alone and the only new mapping is a GetMapping. The two departures from the planned file list both narrow or follow review: no message bundle needed changing, and ubiquitous-language.md was added at the doc-reviewer's explicit direction.

rationale: Read every hunk including the four untracked files. The inversion is id-keyed and mutation-checked by a test, the new route is parameterless and read-only, and no message bundle needed touching because all four template keys already exist in all ten locales. Confirm and merge.
